correctness.rationale: For a nonempty-valued path-independent choice function C on all menus of labelled U, |U|<=5, with |C(A)|<=q, the Aizerman-Malishevski representation expresses every such C as the union of highest-priority singleton selections from a finite family of strict linear orders. Its converse is verified: pointwise OR of priority-maximizers is path independent. Exhaust all subsets of n! orders via exact bitmask union closure (n=5 produces 59386 distinct rules), and for q=1..5 test ALL capacity<=q source rules and ALL q-acceptant targets by inclusion on every menu. Independently authored and compiled a separate C++ exhaustive implementation from the mathematical specification; verified at n=5 source/target counts q1 120/120, q2 13710/480, q3 56140/80, q4 59385/5, q5 59386/1, all zero unexpandable, plus q=3 extension multiplicities 3340,7320,9540,11160,3780,7020,8460,3240,1840,440 for 1,2,4,6,8,10,12,16,24,36 expansions and exactly 39860 law-of-aggregate-demand violations. Verified every generated rule satisfies PI by direct all-menu-pairs test. Prior six-item obstruction reported by Chambers-Yenmez is NOT claimed new. Finite exhaustive proof depends on the classical representation but does NOT assert arbitrarily large |U|.
